about.title: Personal Injury Help in Pacifica, California
about.longDescription: Pacifica's roads carry a steady mix of commuters, coastal visitors, and locals running errands, and that mix shows up in the numbers. In the most recent full year on record, the city saw 80 injury collisions, 106 people hurt, and 2 traffic deaths. Cabrillo Highway, also known as SR-1 or Rt 1, along with Sharp Park Road, account for a large share of the reported crashes, and Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see more activity than other times of the week. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out what comes next can feel overwhelming — medical visits, insurance calls, missed work, and a lot of uncertainty. We provide a free service to help injured people in Pacifica understand their options and get the legal representation they deserve. Our team handles personal injury claims and can look at what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk, and if we take your case, you don't pay unless there's a recovery. Reaching out early can matter, since California law gives most injury claims a limited window to file.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives injury victims two years from the date of the crash to file a claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to move quickly.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the collision, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary injury cases, so compensation for pain and suffering isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. That removes the financial barrier to getting legal help after a crash.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Pacifica?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a city vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months. Talking with our team early helps make sure you don't miss an important filing window.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. We can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Pacifica?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Cabrillo Highway (SR-1/Rt 1) and Sharp Park Road have some of the higher collision counts in the city, and reported crashes tend to peak on Saturdays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency. That means you don't pay legal fees unless we recover money on your behalf.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The specific amount depends on the facts of your case, which we can help assess.
